purpose: Explicit, machine-readable record of which Eve sessions count toward the pre-registered 8-session bar, and why -- so this can never later look like moving the goalposts. See docs/eve_engine_v1_session0_closing_report.md for the full narrative.

pre_registration.eve_must_clear: 5% OOS survival, FDR-corrected, across the full cross-asset family
pre_registration.kill_criterion: if Eve does not clear 5% after 8 (countable) sessions, the open-ended agent approach is falsified and the branch is archived

session_count_provenance.superseded_prior_value_source: docs/investigations/eve_engine_v1_report.md's original 'Pre-registered kill criterion' section, written before the 3 Aug 2026 pre-registration existed
session_count_provenance.reason: The original N=5 was chosen under a ~$1.50/session budget planning figure ('small enough to fit comfortably inside a $20/month ceiling'). Session 0's real spend came in at $0.7129 -- roughly half that -- so at the real per-session cost, ~28 sessions fit inside the $20/month ceiling, not 13, and the original budget constraint that capped N at 5 no longer binds. N=8 fits comfortably and gives a firmer result than N=5 (less exposure to one unusually lucky or unlucky session deciding the outcome). This reconciliation was made and recorded here BEFORE any countable session had run under it -- see docs/investigations/eve_engine_v1_report.md's own appended correction note (original N=5 text left byte-identical, never deleted) for the full narrative.

counting_rule: A session counts toward the pre-registered 8 only once it produces at least one hypothesis that was actually eligible to be scored against real data (i.e. the session ran to completion and the DSL vocabulary / pre-submit validator fix, both landed 2026-08-03, were in place). A session that crashed before completion, or whose every hypothesis was UNTESTABLE_BY_DSL purely because of a since-fixed spec defect (the DSL vocabulary was withheld from Eve, not just strategy examples), produces no data point toward the 5% OOS bar -- an unscoreable hypothesis is not a survival rate of zero, it is an unknown. The 5%/8-session bar itself is UNCHANGED; only what qualifies as a countable session is defined here, before any survival data exists under the fixed system.

Ran to completion (5 turns, 5 web searches, 4 hypotheses proposed, real spend $0.7129) with the tool_result-protocol bug already fixed -- mechanically, everything worked, and Eve's own reasoning was genuine (she read the graveyard's 13 failure patterns, searched real research, justified each idea against a specific prior failure, and dropped one idea herself as not DSL-expressible). But all 4 hypotheses came back UNTESTABLE_BY_DSL, and the cause was purely KEY-NAME mismatches the DSL itself supported (3 used 'compare_to' where the parser requires 'compare_to_field'; 1 used a nested {"stop_loss": {...}} where the parser requires the flat stop_atr_multiple). The original spec deliberately withheld Adam's schema so Eve would think freely rather than fill in a form -- correct intent, wrong scope: withholding the VOCABULARY is different from withholding the CONSTRAINTS. She needed a dictionary, not permission. That is a spec defect on this project's side, not a finding about Eve's capability -- so this session produces no data point toward the 5% OOS bar. Fixed same-day: nero_core.eve.session now supplies the exact DSL vocabulary (ALLOWED_FIELDS, ALLOWED_OPS, exact key names, one worked example) in the system prompt, plus a pre-submit validator that returns the parser's own error and offers up to 2 correction retries before finalizing a hypothesis as UNTESTABLE_BY_DSL. This same amendment is recorded directly on the session's own file at docs/site_data/eve_sessions/eve-20260803T095520Z-394385c7.json (session_label / counts_toward_pre_registered_8 / excluded_from_pre_registration_reason fields, added 2026-08-03).

Ran to completion (6 turns, 3 web searches, 6 hypotheses proposed, real spend $0.4834, terminated via end_session_called -- not a budget stop) with the DSL vocabulary fix already in place from Session 0's own fix. That fix held completely: all 6 propose_hypothesis calls parsed on their first attempt (0 UNTESTABLE_BY_DSL, 0 pre-submit-validator correction attempts needed -- confirms the vocabulary block, not luck, closed Session 0's gap). But all 6 hypotheses targeted an (asset, timeframe) pair OUTSIDE nero_core.asset_universe.APPROVED_RESEARCH_UNIVERSE (only (BTC,4h)/(ETH,4h)/(SOL,4h)/(PAXG,4h) have a research export + computed random-hypothesis baseline) -- GOLD/1week, SILVER/1week, MSFT/1day, USD/JPY/1day, and a malformed 'BTC/4h' asset-field value that didn't even match ('BTC/4h','4h') as a valid pair. Every hypothesis was therefore refused real backtest scoring (candle_data_source='refused') before ever reaching auto_tester.test_hypothesis -- 6/6 DSL-testable, 0/6 actually scored, all verdict_is/verdict_oos null. Same reasoning as Session 0: an unscoreable hypothesis is an unknown, not a survival rate of zero, and the cause was outside Eve's control -- she was never told which pairs this platform can actually backtest. Fixed same-day: nero_core.eve.session's system prompt now states the exact APPROVED_RESEARCH_UNIVERSE list, framed as available data (not permitted ideas) -- she may still propose on any pair; anything outside the list is still recorded honestly as refused, since whether her reasoning consistently reaches for pairs this platform lacks is itself useful signal about what data to acquire next. This session produces no data point toward the 5% OOS bar; the pre-registered 8 still has not started.

First real attempt at the first countable session, run after the items-3/4/5/7 precondition fixes (generated_at server-side injection, frequency-gate/SURVIVED-bar prompt additions) and the CC-1 self-dedup/run-summary-persistence fixes all landed. Crashed on turn 0 with a real requests.exceptions.ReadTimeout against api.anthropic.com (120s claude_timeout_seconds ceiling -- see llm_client.py's LlmParameters docstring; this is the SAME failure mode Session 0's own two earliest crashed attempts hit at the OLD 60s ceiling, confirming 120s is not always sufficient either). ReadTimeout is not one of RejectedBeforeTokenProcessingError's 401/403/429 codes, so session.py's own except clause does not catch it -- it propagates uncaught through pipeline.run_pipeline's except-Exception path (which sends exactly one ntfy failure notification, then re-raises) and crashes the invoking script. No session record file was ever written (session.run_session crashed before its own end-of-function write). One orphaned 'reserved' budget-ledger entry exists (turn_index=0, $0.0983 projected, never reconciled -- conservatively counted at that projected value against the month/session ceilings per budget_ledger.py's own RESERVE-THEN-RECONCILE design until reconciled or released; NOT released, since release_entry is only ever called for a confirmed-$0 401/403/429 rejection, and a ReadTimeout's real outcome is genuinely unknown). Per explicit standing instruction ('do not retry on failure'), this attempt was NOT immediately retried. Machinery failure, not an Eve result -- produces no data point toward the 5% OOS bar, same classification as Session 0's own earlier ReadTimeout crashes.
